JAIPUR WAS DESIGNED— in 1727 —
Satellite: Sentinel-2 cloudless 2016 by EOX (CC BY 4.0) · Map data © OpenStreetMap · plan: supplied diagram fitted to OSM streets
Jaipur was designed
300 years ago on
paper.
In 1727, Maharaja
Sawai Jai Singh II
decided to move his
capital down from Amer
fort.
And he gave the job to
a young architect from
Bengal Vidyadhar
Bhattacharya.
Vidyadhar used the
ancient Vastu Shastra
a grid of nine
squares, like a
mandala.
Each block became a
neighbourhood,
for a trade or a
community.
The palace sits right
in the centre.
Then the roads.
Three wide streets
east to west,
crossed by streets
north to south.
Where they meet the
great chaupars:
Badi Chaupar,
Choti Chaupar once
with water tanks in
the middle.
All of it inside a
city wall,
with seven gates.
And in 1876,
the whole city was
painted pink to
welcome the Prince of
Wales which is why
we're the Pink City.
In 2019, UNESCO
declared the walled
city a World Heritage
Site for its planning.
And the planning
didn't stop.
C-Scheme and MI Road
in the 1940s.
Then Malviya Nagar,
Jawahar Nagar,
and Vidyadhar Nagar
named after the
architect himself.
Then Mansarovar,
one of Jaipur's
biggest planned
colonies.
And today the Ring
Road and the Metro.
300 years later,
Jaipur is still
growing on a plan.
Send this to someone
who loves Jaipur and
tell me in the
comments:
which area do you live
in?
